result.title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
result.summary: Large Language Model training is increasingly constrained by memory capacity. Activation Checkpointing reduces activation memory by avoiding storing selected activations during the forward pass and rematerializing them during backpropagation, thereby trading memory savings for additional computation. Although this technique is essential for scaling model training, rematerialization can be prohibitively expensive, particularly for Transformer linear layers. Approximate computation could reduce this overhead, but conventional approaches either introduce errors that accumulate over the backward pass or fail to exploit information available from the initial forward pass. We introduce a novel approximate rematerialization method that can yield unbiased gradient estimates: using information collected during the initial forward pass, the method selectively recomputes only the most important layer components, either through greedy selection or randomized sketching. Ablation studies show that the resulting gradients closely match the exact gradients. When applied to feed-forward layers, attention layers, or both, our method can recompute only two-thirds of the layer components in a Llama-488M model, while increasing perplexity by just 1.7%, 1.2%, and 2.5%, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种近似重计算方法：利用前向传播中已收集的信息，以贪心选择或随机草图只重算 Transformer 层中最关键的组件，从而在反向传播时以较低计算代价获得近似无偏的梯度。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但其依据前向统计筛选「重要组件」并按需重算、同时用随机草图控制偏差的思路，可能为 latent 状态的按需刷新与视觉证据筛选提供计算价值分配的借鉴线索。
